label: Tattoos and piercings
description: Tattoo styles and placements, named body piercings, henna and decorative scarification.
notes: Permanent tattoos, named piercings and lasting or temporary decorative skin markings belong here. Values use familiar style or placement names that fit after with, without implying the wearer’s descent. Applied facial cosmetics and theatrical fake wounds belong in person.makeup, while removable jewelry belongs in person.accessory. Tattoo styles describe linework and shading, placement entries describe coverage, and piercing entries name the visible location.

values.look: Bold black outlines enclose flat red, green and yellow motifs such as roses, anchors and swallows.
Heavy outlines surround ornate flowers or animals with layered shading and a broad, rich color palette.
Thin, delicate outlines form small detailed designs with little solid fill or shading.
Solid black shapes and bold high-contrast patterns cover areas of otherwise bare skin.
Closely spaced dots build shaded patterns and gradients instead of continuous blocks of ink.
Interlocking polygons, circles and precise repeating lines form structured patterns on the skin.
Dense colored dragons, koi or peonies wrap the arm against dark waves, clouds and wind bars.
Bold black bands combine repeating triangles, chevrons and curved motifs around the limbs or torso.
Dark curving lines and spiral motifs follow the contours of the cheeks, forehead and chin.
A carefully shaded human face appears photographic rather than outlined or cartoonlike.
Translucent-looking colored washes, soft bleeding edges and splashes surround a tattoo motif.
Black ink and smooth gray shading create depth without colored pigment.
Detailed drawn scenes use visible contour lines and hatching like an ink illustration on skin.
Shaded pipes, pistons and cables appear embedded beneath torn-skin shapes.
Large continuous areas of opaque black ink cover most of an arm or leg, sometimes leaving bare-skin gaps.
Readable words or names are tattooed in prominent script or block lettering.
One small isolated symbol or design sits at the wrist, with most surrounding skin bare.
One large continuous composition spans the upper and lower back from shoulder to shoulder.
Many separate small tattoos scatter over the arm with visible gaps of bare skin between them.
A broad design spans the upper chest below the collarbones.
Small letters or symbols form a row across the finger knuckles.
A prominent design covers the front or side of the neck above the clothing neckline.
Small studs or hoops pass through the soft lower lobes of the ears.
A ring or horseshoe-shaped bar hangs from the center of the nose between the nostrils.
A small stud or fitted hoop sits through the side of one nostril.
A small ring or stud passes through the outer upper rim of the ear.
A long straight bar crosses the upper ear and joins two cartilage piercings.
A small stud or ring sits in the cartilage flap directly in front of the ear canal.
A curved bar or ring passes through the outer eyebrow, showing jewelry above and below it.
A single stud sits centered below the lower lip, above the chin.
Large plugs or tunnels fill widened holes in the earlobes, visibly expanding the lobes.
Two ends of a curved bar show at the center of the lower lip and directly beneath it.
Matching studs or rings sit beneath the lower lip, one near each corner of the mouth.
A single stud sits in the central groove between the upper lip and the nose.
A horizontal bar shows one bead on each side of the bridge of the nose, between the eyes.
A small hoop passes through the innermost ear cartilage fold above the ear canal.
A stud sits in the central bowl of the ear, or a ring circles from that bowl around the outer ear.
A curved bar with a bead or dangling ornament sits through the upper rim of the navel.
Reddish-brown floral and paisley lines cover the palms, fingers or backs of the hands.
Raised, skin-colored scars form deliberate geometric lines or repeated patterns on the skin.
